activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The blue bag is cheaper than the brown bag. (AS)

evaluator.answer: The brown bag is not as cheap as the blue bag

activities.explanation: The comparative «cheaper than» becomes «not as cheap as» when the subject order changes.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: Someone cleans the office every evening. (CLEANED)

evaluator.answer: The office is cleaned every evening

activities.explanation: The present simple passive is «is cleaned» when the focus is the office.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: “I am ready,” Sam said. (THAT)

evaluator.answer: Sam said that he was ready

activities.explanation: The pronoun changes from «I» to «he» and «am» backshifts to «was».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: I started learning Spanish in 2023. (SINCE)

evaluator.answer: I have learned Spanish since 2023

activities.explanation: A starting year can be expressed with present perfect plus «since».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The suitcase is too heavy for Mia to lift. (ENOUGH)

evaluator.answer: The suitcase is not light enough for Mia to lift

activities.explanation: «Too heavy» can be reformulated as «not light enough» while keeping the result.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The train journey takes longer than the bus journey. (QUICK)

evaluator.answer: The bus journey is quicker than the train journey

activities.explanation: The comparison changes the subject and uses the adjective «quick».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: They built this bridge in 1998. (BUILT)

evaluator.answer: This bridge was built in 1998

activities.explanation: The past simple passive is «was built».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: “We will call you tomorrow,” the nurse said. (WOULD)

evaluator.answer: The nurse said that they would call me the next day

activities.explanation: «Will» becomes «would», «you» becomes «me», and «tomorrow» becomes «the next day».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: I have not visited the museum for two years. (LAST)

evaluator.answer: The last time I visited the museum was two years ago

activities.explanation: «For two years» can be expressed as the time since the last visit.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The room is too small for six people. (ENOUGH)

evaluator.answer: The room is not big enough for six people

activities.explanation: «Too small» becomes «not big enough» when the intended result is impossible accommodation.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: People say that the café serves the best soup in town. (SAID)

evaluator.answer: It is said that the café serves the best soup in town

activities.explanation: An impersonal reporting passive uses «It is said that».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The red route is less difficult than the blue route. (AS)

evaluator.answer: The blue route is not as easy as the red route

activities.explanation: The equivalent comparison changes «less difficult» into «not as easy».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The technician has repaired my laptop. (BEEN)

evaluator.answer: My laptop has been repaired by the technician

activities.explanation: The present perfect passive is «has been repaired».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: “I can meet you after work,” Noor told me. (COULD)

evaluator.answer: Noor told me that she could meet me after work

activities.explanation: «Can» backshifts to «could», and both pronouns follow the new reporting perspective.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: I began working at the shop three months ago. (FOR)

evaluator.answer: I have worked at the shop for three months

activities.explanation: The duration is expressed with present perfect and «for three months».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The storm was so strong that the ferry could not sail. (TOO)

evaluator.answer: The storm was too strong for the ferry to sail

activities.explanation: The result clause becomes «too strong for ... to sail».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: Someone must approve the form before Friday. (APPROVED)

evaluator.answer: The form must be approved before Friday

activities.explanation: The modal passive is «must be approved».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: “I have finished the report,” Eli said. (HAD)

evaluator.answer: Eli said that he had finished the report

activities.explanation: The present perfect backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The last time we ate at that restaurant was in June. (SINCE)

evaluator.answer: We have not eaten at that restaurant since June

activities.explanation: «Since June» gives the point from which the negative period continues.

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The lecture was so interesting that everyone stayed until the end. (SUCH)

evaluator.answer: It was such an interesting lecture that everyone stayed until the end

activities.explanation: The adjective phrase becomes «such an interesting lecture».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: People believe that the painting was made by a local artist. (BELIEVED)

evaluator.answer: The painting is believed to have been made by a local artist

activities.explanation: The reporting passive with a completed past action uses «is believed to have been made».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The green route is considerably less demanding than the mountain path. (NEARLY)

evaluator.answer: The mountain path is not nearly as easy as the green route

activities.explanation: The stronger comparison is preserved with «not nearly as easy as».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: “I may arrive late because the road is closed,” Jo said. (MIGHT)

evaluator.answer: Jo said that she might arrive late because the road was closed

activities.explanation: «May» can backshift to «might», and the reporting context changes «is» to «was».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: The technician repaired the machine while it was still under warranty. (REPAIRED)

evaluator.answer: The machine was repaired by the technician while it was still under warranty

activities.explanation: The object becomes the subject of the past simple passive «was repaired».

activities.instructions: Rewrite the sentence using the words in brackets.
activities.prompt: I regret not checking the platform number earlier. (WISH)

evaluator.answer: I wish I had checked the platform number earlier

activities.explanation: Regret about a past action uses «wish + past perfect».
